subject: a question on how to include weights

messages.author: b0b6a951c5f3de59
messages.subject: a question on how to include weights
parts:
Dear stan developers,

Thank you for reading this email! I plan to fit a model as follows:

E(y)=b0+b1*(w1*x1+w2*x2+(1-w1-w2)*x3)

where b0 and b1 are coefficients, w1, w2 and (1-w1-w2) are weights for x1, x2, and x3. I write a stan code for it. But I am not sure whether it is efficient or not. Could you give some suggestions on how to correct or improve the code? Thank you!

Regards,

Li

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: a question on how to include weights
parts:
On Monday, November 28, 2016 at 11:09:52 AM UTC-5, lyly...@connect.hku.hk wrote:
Dear stan developers,

Thank you for reading this email! I plan to fit a model as follows:

E(y)=b0+b1*(w1*x1+w2*x2+(1-w1-w2)*x3)

where b0 and b1 are coefficients, w1, w2 and (1-w1-w2) are weights for x1, x2, and x3. I write a stan code for it. But I am not sure whether it is efficient or not. Could you give some suggestions on how to correct or improve the code? Thank you!

Presuming that you want w1 > 0, w2 > 0, and w3 = 1 - w1 - w2 > 0, then you need to do in the parameters block

simplex[3] w;

instead of

real<lower=0,upper=1> w1;
real<lower=0,upper=1> w2;

and then get rid of the uniform priors on w1 and w2. Use w[1] for w1, etc.

Ben
